title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pages 90-92). The base is S_0 = Spec Z[1/2], and S̃_0 = S_0[μ_4^×] = Spec Z[1/2,i]. U_{0,3} (also written M_{0,3}) is the Legendre λ-line P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It carries the Legendre family y^2 = x(x−1)(x−t). The group D_3 ≅ S_3 acts on U_{0,3} through the anharmonic substitutions, i.e. by permuting {0,1,∞}. An extra factor μ_4 acts on the μ_4^× component.

The problem served is to compare two actions of (g,λ) ∈ D_3 × μ_4 on sections of the 'weight' bundles O(k) over U_{0,3} × μ_4^×. Here O(1) is in effect the Hodge bundle ω of the Legendre curve, with ξ = dx/y.
- The tautological action is (g,λ).ξ, induced by the canonical substitution.
- The modular action is T_{g,λ}, given by transport of structure on the elliptic curve.
The page records the comparison:
- (51) T_{g,λ} ξ = λ·(g,λ).ξ for ξ ∈ Γ(O(1))(t).
- (52) T_{g,λ} η = λ^2 (g,λ).η for η ∈ Γ(O(2))(t), by taking squares.
- (53) T_{g,λ} τ = λ^2 sg(g)·(g,λ).τ for τ of 'weight 2 twisted by the sign'. τ is very plausibly a section of Ω^1_{U_{0,3}}, via a Kodaira–Spencer-type identification of ω^{⊗2} with differentials, which is only S_3-equivariant up to the sign character.

The factor λ ∈ μ_4 is classical. For example, the substitution x ↦ 1−x turns y^2 = x(x−1)(x−t) into y^2 = −x(x−1)(x−(1−t)), so one needs y ↦ iy and dx/y picks up a factor ±i.

Restriction to D'_3. Let D'_3 = {(g,λ): λ^2 = sg(g)} ⊂ D_3 × μ_4. On the previous page this is the subgroup preserving 'direct' Legendre–Jacobi pinnings.
- Even g have λ = ±1 and odd g have λ = ±i, so |D'_3| = 12.
- The projection (g,λ) ↦ λ is a surjective character to μ_4 with kernel A_3 ≅ Z/3.
- Hence D'_3 ≅ Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, the dicyclic group Dic_3, with abelianization ≅ μ_4. This is (54), and χ_4(g,λ) = λ.
- Over S_0 this is a twisted (non-constant) finite étale group scheme, since μ_4 is not constant over Z[1/2]. It becomes constant over S̃_0.

Substituting λ^2 = sg(g) gives:
- (51bis) T_g ξ = χ_4(g)·g.ξ.
- (52bis) T_g η = sg(g^0)·g.η, where g^0 is the image of g in S_3.
- (53bis) T_g τ = g.τ, so the modular and tautological actions agree on the twisted weight-2 objects. This fits τ being differential forms on U_{0,3}.

Modern reading. D'_3 is SL_2(Z)/Γ for the normal subgroup Γ = {γ ∈ Γ(2): a ≡ 1 mod 4} ≅ Γ(2)/{±1}, which is torsion-free and conjugate to Γ_1(4) by τ ↦ 2τ. So a 'direct Legendre–Jacobi pinning' is a rigidified, −1-killing refinement of level 2. That is why U_{0,3} over S̃_0 is a fine moduli scheme. χ_4 is the reduction mod 4 of the abelianization SL_2(Z)^ab ≅ Z/12.

The next page goes on to define Jacobi pinnings of level 4 relative to level 2.
errors: No mathematical error found. Formulas (51bis)-(53bis) follow correctly from (51)-(53) under λ^2 = sg(g).
The notation is loose: in (52bis) 'sg(g^0)' means the sign of the image of g in S_3, while elsewhere sg(g) is used for the same thing.
The precise bundle in the margin of (53) is unreadable, so the meaning of τ is inferred, not certain.

ideas.what: Comparison of the modular (transport-of-structure) action with the tautological geometric action on weight-k bundles over the Legendre line, with explicit characters λ, λ^2, λ^2·sg.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphy factors / equivariant structure of the Hodge bundle ω^k on the level-2 modular curve; S_3 action on Legendre forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi; Klein for the anharmonic group); scheme-theoretic versions in Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur, and later tmf(2) computations (e.g. Stojanoska)

ideas.what: The group D'_3 = {(g,λ) ∈ S_3 × μ_4 : λ^2 = sg(g)}, a twisted form over Z[1/2] of the dicyclic group of order 12, with abelianization μ_4 and canonical character χ_4.
ideas.modern_name: Dic_3 ≅ SL_2(Z)/(Γ(2) ∩ {a≡1 mod 4}); 4-part of the abelianization Z/12 of SL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory / modular group folklore

ideas.what: Twisted weight-2 objects (probably differentials, via Kodaira–Spencer) on which the modular and geometric actions coincide (53bis).
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1(log cusps), equivariant up to the sign/determinant character

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine bookkeeping computation of characters, classical in substance: the S_3 action on Legendre forms, the factor i on dx/y, and Dic_3 as a quotient of SL_2(Z). The only mildly distinctive feature is the treatment over Z[1/2] with D'_3 as a non-constant twisted group scheme, rigidifying level 2 via μ_4. This is equivalent to the known Γ_1(4)-type fine moduli and is standard in later literature.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed as 𝕳_4 / ℍ_4 in (54) and in 'D'_{3ab} ≃ ℍ_4' is almost certainly μ_4, Grothendieck's double-struck μ, consistent with the neighbouring pages. The note reads '(étant donné que D'_{3,ab} ≃ μ_4)'.
In the margins of (51)-(53) the subscript is U_{0,3}, as on the neighbouring pages, rather than M_{0,3}. The margins read something like 'ξ ∈ Γ(O_{U_{0,3}}(1))(t)' and 'η ∈ Γ(O_{U_{0,3}}(2))(t)'.
The margin of (53) has a corrected bundle, apparently with a second line 'O_{U_{0,3}}(2)…'. It plausibly involves Ω^1 or a sign twist, not plain O(2), as the extra sg(g) in (53) requires.
In (51) the scratched text after λ is a deleted 'sg(g)', correctly marked as deleted.
In (52bis) the image reads 'sg(g°)' (g with a superscript circle); the transcription is correct.
The opening phrase 'pour la substitution canonique' is overlined, i.e. inserted. The '10' at the top is a margin or section marker, not part of the formula.
